title: Launch Chronograph & Release Lattice Orchestration for Runtime/Console/API
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current launch calendar is optimized for single-surface rollouts and does not support coordinated multi-surface releases across runtime, console, and API with staggered regional capacity. This causes last-minute rework, unclear ownership, and manual capacity hedging.

Goal: Build a repeatable 'chronograph' planning pattern and a release lattice orchestration playbook that standardizes gating, capacity reservations, canary phasing, and communications across runtime, console, and API teams so we can safely run 3x concurrent release trains while preserving latency and availability SLOs.

This ticket scopes the PM-level orchestration plan, stakeholder assignments, gating matrix, and the initial cadence template for Q2–Q3 2026 launches.
acceptance_criteria: Consolidated launch cadence template delivered with per-surface signal definitions (runtime/console/api)
Gating matrix completed with owner for each gate and explicit rollback criteria
Capacity hedge playbook documented with reserved burst lanes and cost-accounting tags
Communication runbook published with templated stakeholder notices and escalation steps
Pilot launch schedule for runtime-1.20 + console-2026.04 + api-compat-3.1 mapped into calendar and approved by stakeholders
milestones: Capacity hedge sign-off w/ infra finance: 2026-04-01
risks: Insufficient reserved capacity causing post-canary throttles and customer-facing latency spikes
Overlapping rollout windows across regions that exceed ops on-call capacity
Unclear rollback ownership between runtime and API teams leading to delayed mitigation
Financial exposure from untracked burst capacity during emergency hedges
deliverables: Release Lattice playbook (gates, signals, rollback criteria)
Capacity hedge runbook and finance tagging map
Comms templates for preflight, canary, rollback, and GA
Pilot launch schedule and postmortem template
comms_plan: Preflight 2 weeks before pilot: product and infra stakeholders. Daily readiness check 72/48/24 hours. Canary start/stop notices published to #launch-announcements and email owners. Escalation matrix: on-call SRE -> Eng lead -> PM -> Exec if SLOs violated for >15 minutes. Post-pilot report published within 48 hours.
metrics: Customer-facing latency p50/p95 for text-gen across runtime: target no regression >5%
Error budget consumption for API surface: <= 10% during canary
Console critical-path load time: no regressions compared to baseline
Token cost delta observed vs. forecast during pilot
Rollforward/rollback frequency and mean time to mitigate
notes_and_updates: 2026-03-01: Initial draft created; scoped to runtime/console/api pilot. Assigned Jonah for coordination.
2026-03-08: SRE flagged on-call capacity conflict for 2026-04-22; proposed shifting Region A by +6 hours to reduce overlap.
2026-03-12: Infra Finance requested cost projection for burst lanes—ENG-80123 assigned to produce estimates.

2026-03-15: Stakeholder sync: agreed to a layered rollback ownership (runtime owns model-serving rollbacks; API owns surface-level throttles; Console owns UI feature flags). Updated gating matrix to reflect ownership.
